  - region "Simple English explanation of Collinearity Using Coordinate Area":
    - group:

      - heading "Understand Collinearity Using Coordinate Area" [level=2]
  - text: CLASS 10 · COORDINATE GEOMETRY
  - heading "Collinearity Using Coordinate Area" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Test whether three points are collinear by calculating the area of the triangle they form.
  - navigation:
    - button "INTERACT"
    - button "LEARN"
    - button "EXAMPLE"
    - button "FORMULA"
    - button "PRACTICE"
  - complementary: "ⓘ Rule: Three points A, B, C are collinear if and only if the area of △ABC is 0. Determinant Signed area Zero-area snap"
  - main:
    - complementary:
      - heading "Move points A, B and C" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Drag the points on the plane or edit their coordinates.
      - text: ● A x
      - spinbutton "Collinearity A x": "1"
      - text: "y"
      - spinbutton "Collinearity A y": "2"
      - button "Reset point A":
        - img
      - text: ● B x
      - spinbutton "Collinearity B x": "3"
      - text: "y"
      - spinbutton "Collinearity B y": "4"
      - button "Reset point B":
        - img
      - text: ● C x
      - spinbutton "Collinearity C x": "5"
      - text: "y"
      - spinbutton "Collinearity C y": "6"
      - button "Reset point C":
        - img
      - heading "Determinant (2 × Area)" [level=3]
      - strong: D = |x₁ y₁ 1; x₂ y₂ 1; x₃ y₃ 1| = 0
      - heading "Area of △ABC" [level=3]
      - strong: A = |D|/2 = 0
      - heading "Signed area gauge" [level=3]
      - text: "0"
      - emphasis: ✓ Exactly zero
      - heading "Collinearity result" [level=3]
      - strong: ✓ Collinear
      - text: Area = 0 → Points lie on a straight line. Show line-fit
      - checkbox "Show line fit" [checked]
      - button "🧲 Snap C to line AB (area = 0)"
    - article:
      - button "Select tool":
        - img
      - button "Pan tool":
        - img
      - button "Delete point C":
        - img
      - text: Zoom
      - button "Zoom out":
        - img
      - text: 100%
      - button "Zoom in":
        - img
      - img "Draggable collinearity coordinate plane": A(1, 2) B(3, 4) C(5, 6)
      - text: Distance of C from line AB (perpendicular)
      - strong: d = 0.0000
      - text: "Interpretation: d = 0 Point C lies on line AB."
    - article:
      - heading "💡 Why it works" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "Twice the signed area of △ABC is the determinant:"
      - strong: D=x₁(y₂−y₃)+x₂(y₃−y₁)+x₃(y₁−y₂).
      - paragraph: If D=0, then A=|D|/2=0, so the points are collinear.
    - article:
      - heading "▣ Worked example" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A(1,2), B(3,4), C(5,6)
      - strong: D = 1(4−6)+3(6−2)+5(2−4) = 0
      - paragraph: A=|0|/2=0
      - emphasis: "Result: Collinear ✓"
    - article:
      - heading "⚠ Common misconception" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A very small area ≠ exactly zero.
      - paragraph: Floating-point rounding can make a tiny area look like zero.
      - paragraph: Use zero-area snap or check that D=0 exactly.
    - 'heading "◴ Challenge: Make the points collinear" [level=2]'
    - paragraph: Move point C anywhere, then drag it so that the area becomes exactly zero. When collinear, give the equation of the line through A and B.
    - article:
      - heading "Your line equation" [level=3]
      - textbox "Line equation":
        - /placeholder: y = mx + c
      - button "Check answer"
    - article:
      - heading "Hint" [level=3]
      - paragraph: The line through A(1,2) and B(3,4) has slope m=(4−2)/(3−1)=1.
      - paragraph: Use point-slope or slope-intercept form.
    - article:
      - heading "Progress" [level=3]
      - paragraph: ◉ Area = 0
      - paragraph: ◉ Line-fit passes through all three points
      - paragraph: ○ Equation is correct
      - emphasis: Ready to check
